dedupe_keys.name: hardware in the loop cybersecurity assessment against false data injection attacks in renewable plants

description: The source describes a photovoltaic plant digitally replicated in OPAL-RT and controlled through its real ICT and OT equipment at the University of Sevilla. A state-estimator-based false-data identification tool is integrated into the plant control system and assessed with unitary and daily-profile laboratory tests. The deposited book chapter was under first review from 6 July 2026; publication date does not establish peer-review completion. This is a controlled laboratory application, with field deployment and independent operational performance unknown. It is distinct from the energy-community multi-plant test and from the detection algorithm itself. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected; no measurements, archives, source code or document bodies were retrieved. Public access and the deposit document licence do not establish executable access, software reuse rights or operating costs. Coverage remains bounded to the named experiments, with other geographic and temporal fields unknown. Related project resources may overlap; common project membership does not establish identical simulation inputs or results.
name: Hardware-in-the-Loop Cybersecurity Assessment Against False Data Injection Attacks in Renewable Plants
